CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with a history of kidney stones. Approximately one week ago, while working in the barn moving hay, he developed sudden onset severe pain in his right back. He states the pain radiated almost down to the groin. Associated symptoms included diaphoresis and nausea. He saw his PCP who ordered a CT scan that confirmed a kidney stone. Since the initial episode, he has had a couple of episodes of pain that did not last as long. He denies hematuria or darker urine. He has been straining his urine as instructed and has not visualized any stone fragments. Denies current pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for initial diaphoresis and nausea associated with pain episode. Denies hematuria or dark urine. No fever reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No prior kidney stones.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Father has a history of kidney stones.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works with horses in a barn, moving hay.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: normal, no fever. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Abdomen: no tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. CVA tenderness on the right side.

RESULTS
CT scan shows a stone measuring 0.5 centimeters located in the proximal right ureter. No evidence of hydronephrosis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right ureteral kidney stone (proximal right ureter, 0.5 cm). Plan: increase fluid intake to facilitate passage of stone. Prescribe oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours for pain; may use acetaminophen between doses for breakthrough pain. Continue urine straining. Order BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to assess for infection and determine need for antibiotics. Follow-up in 1-2 weeks. If stone has not passed, discuss further treatment options including lithotripsy.
